```{r include = FALSE}
Data_dir <- "../Data/"
Code_dir <- "../Code"
Plot_dir <- "../Plots/"

# note: unstandardized questionnaire data for descriptive stats and plotting ('us' stands for 'unstandardized')
questionnaire_us_study1 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "questionnaire_us_study1.csv"))
questionnaire_us_study2 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "questionnaire_us_study2.csv"))

# note: hr stands for 'horizon', referring to the Horizon task
hr_long_study1 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "hr_long_study1.csv")) # behavioral data in long format
hr_wide_study1 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "hr_wide_study1.csv")) # behavioral data in wide format
hr_mb_study1 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "hr_mb_study1.csv")) # computational modeling data in wide format

hr_long_study2 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "hr_long_study2.csv")) # behavioral data in long format
hr_wide_study2 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "hr_wide_study2.csv")) # behavioral data in wide format
hr_mb_study2 <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "hr_mb_study2.csv")) # computational modeling data in wide format

# note: tr stands for 'tree', referring to the Orchard task
tr_long <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "tr_long.csv")) 
tr_wide <- read.csv(file.path(Data_dir, "tr_wide.csv"))
```

# Pearson correlations
### scales correlations (**SI table 1 & 2**)
Refer to the output file "scales_study1_cor_matrix.csv" and "scales_study2_cor_matrix.csv" for the results
```{r eval=FALSE}
scales_study1 <- c('unpredictability', 'digit_span', 'family_income', 'life_events', 'child_anxiety')
scales_study2 <- c('unpredictability', 'digit_span', 'family_income', 'perceived_stress')

get_correlation_fun("study1", scales_study1)
get_correlation_fun("study2", scales_study2)
```

### QUIC subscales (**SI table 3 & 4**)
Refer to the output file "quic_study1_cor_matrix.csv" and "quic_study2_cor_matrix.csv" for the results
```{r eval=FALSE}
quic_study1 <- c("parental_monitoring", "parental_predictability", "parental_environment", "physical_environment", "safety_and_security")
quic_study2 <- c("parental_monitoring", "parental_predictability", "parental_environment", "physical_environment", "safety_and_security")

get_correlation_fun("study1", quic_study1)
get_correlation_fun("study2", quic_study2)
```

# Model-based Analysis
### Horizon task directed exploration
```{r}
df1 <- hr_mb_study1 %>% left_join(., subset(hr_wide_study1, select = c("id", "child_anxiety")))
df2 <- hr_mb_study2 %>% left_join(., subset(hr_wide_study2, select = c("id", "perceived_stress")))

### Study 1
summary(lm(mb_directed_exploration ~ unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + child_anxiety, data = df1))

### Study 2
summary(lm(mb_directed_exploration ~ unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + perceived_stress, data = df2))
```

# Additional Mediating Mechanisms for Reduced Exploration in the Horizon Task
### Reaction time
In the model output below, check **unpredictability** for the effect of childhood unpredictability on reaction time for directed exploration; check **horizon:unpredictability** for the effect of childhood unpredictability on reaction time for strategic exploration; check **conflict:unpredictability** for the effect of childhood unpredictability on reaction time for directed exploration in reward-information conflict games.
```{r}
### Study 1
control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e6),check.nobs.vs.nRE = "ignore") 
summary(lmer(reaction_time_c5 ~ horizon*conflict*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + child_anxiety + (1 + horizon + conflict|id), data = hr_long_study1, control = control))

### Study 2
control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e6),check.nobs.vs.nRE = "ignore") 
summary(lmer(reaction_time_c5 ~ horizon*conflict*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + perceived_stress + (1 + horizon + conflict|id), data = hr_long_study2, control = control))
```

### Reward maximization
In the model output below, check **reward_differential:unpredictability** for the effect of childhood unpredictability on reward maximization (choose the high mean option at the last choice in H6 games as a function of reward differential). 
```{r}
### Study 1
control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e7))
mod <- glmer(chose_high_mean_c10_long ~ reward_differential*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + child_anxiety + (1 + reward_differential|id), data = hr_long_study1, family = binomial, control = control)

summary(mod)
tab_model(mod)

### Study 2
control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa",optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e7))
mod <- glmer(chose_high_mean_c10_long ~ reward_differential*unpredictability + digit_span + family_income + perceived_stress + (1 + reward_differential|id), data = hr_long_study2, family = binomial, control = control)

summary(mod)
tab_model(mod)
```

# SI Figure 1
```{r}
### prep data frames
df_plot_study1 <- hr_wide_study1 %>% 
  select(id, choice06:choice10) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("choice"), names_to = "choice", values_to = "chose_high_mean") %>% 
  summarySE(measurevar="chose_high_mean", groupvars=c("choice")) %>% 
  mutate(study = 'Primary Study')

df_plot_study2 <- hr_wide_study2 %>% 
  select(id, choice06:choice10) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("choice"), names_to = "choice", values_to = "chose_high_mean") %>% 
  summarySE(measurevar="chose_high_mean", groupvars=c("choice")) %>% 
  mutate(study = 'Replication Study')

df_plot <- rbind(df_plot_study1, df_plot_study2)

### create line plot
ggplot(df_plot, aes(x=choice, y=chose_high_mean, colour=study, group=study)) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=chose_high_mean-se, ymax=chose_high_mean+se), colour="black", width=.1) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size=3, shape=21, fill="white") + # 21 is filled circle
  xlab("Post-choices for Long Horizon Games") +
  ylab("Choosing High Mean Option") +
  scale_colour_hue(name="Study", breaks=c("LIA", "EXP")) +
  theme_bw() +
  ylim(0.5,1.0) + 
  scale_color_discrete(labels = c("Primary Study", "Replication Study")) +
  theme(legend.justification = "top")
ggsave(filename = file.path(Plot_dir,"SI_Figure1.png"), width = 15, height = 10, units = "cm")
```

# SI Figure 2
```{r}
# scale distribution
hist_quic_study1 <- questionnaire_us_study1 %>% 
  select(parental_monitoring:safety_and_security, unpredictability) %>% 
  rename("Parental Monitoring" = parental_monitoring,
         "Parental Predictability" = parental_predictability,
         "Parental Environment" = parental_environment,
         "Physical Environment" = physical_environment,
         "Safety and Security" = safety_and_security,
         "Total Score" = unpredictability) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) + 
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  geom_histogram(position="dodge", alpha=0.5) +
  theme(legend.position="top") +
  theme_bw()
hist_quic_study1
```

# SI Figure 3
```{r}
### select those whose total quic score is higher than 10 (~ top 20%)
quic_top_study1 <- questionnaire_us_study1 %>% 
  select(id, parental_monitoring:safety_and_security, unpredictability) %>% 
  rename("Parental Monitoring" = parental_monitoring,
         "Parental Predictability" = parental_predictability,
         "Parental Environment" = parental_environment,
         "Physical Environment" = physical_environment,
         "Safety and Security" = safety_and_security) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, ~(scale(.) %>% as.vector)) %>% 
  filter(unpredictability >= .80) %>% select(-unpredictability) %>% # this cutoff separates the top 20%
  pivot_longer(cols = !id, names_to = "subscales", values_to = "values")

quic_top_study2 <- questionnaire_us_study2 %>% 
  mutate(id = as.character(id)) %>% 
  select(id, parental_monitoring:safety_and_security, unpredictability) %>% 
  rename("Parental Monitoring" = parental_monitoring,
         "Parental Predictability" = parental_predictability,
         "Parental Environment" = parental_environment,
         "Physical Environment" = physical_environment,
         "Safety and Security" = safety_and_security) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, ~(scale(.) %>% as.vector)) %>% 
  filter(unpredictability >= .80) %>% select(-unpredictability) %>% # this cutoff separates the top 20%
  pivot_longer(cols = !id, names_to = "subscales", values_to = "values")

### make the plot
ggplot(data = quic_top_study1, aes(x = subscales, y = values, group = id, color = id)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() +  
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(10)) + # wrap the x axis labels
  guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Subject ID")) + # change the legend title
  labs(x ="QUIC Subscales", y = "Standardized Values") # change axis titles
ggsave(filename = file.path(Plot_dir,"quic_spaghetti_study1.png"), width = 20, height = 15, units = "cm")

ggplot(data = quic_top_study2, aes(x = subscales, y = values, group = id, color = id)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() +  
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(10)) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(title = "Subject ID")) + # change the legend title
  labs(x ="QUIC Subscales", y = "Standardized Values") # change axis titles
ggsave(filename = file.path(Plot_dir,"quic_spaghetti_study2.png"), width = 20, height = 15, units = "cm")
```
